claims.question: q1
claims.claim: A semantic compiler resolves business metrics into governed SQL at compile time and injects policies before the warehouse is touched.
claims.quote: A [semantic compiler](https://colrows.com/docs/saas/) resolves your business metrics into governed SQL at compile time, with policies injected before the warehouse is touched.

claims.question: q2
claims.claim: In a cited study, GPT-4 zero-shot on an enterprise insurance schema scored 16.7% overall and 0% on high-schema-complexity questions, while the same questions over a knowledge-graph representation reached 54.2%.
claims.quote: The [Sequeda, Allemang and Jacob study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.07509) isolated this variable: GPT-4 zero-shot on an enterprise insurance schema scored 16.7%, and on the high-schema-complexity questions, **0%**. The same questions over a knowledge-graph representation of the same database: 54.2%. Nothing about the model changed. The available meaning did.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On Spider 2.0, an o1-preview-based agent framework solved 21.3% versus 91.2% on Spider 1.0, and GPT-4o scored 10.1% versus 86.6%, an 8.5x collapse.
claims.quote: The authors' o1-preview-based agent framework solved **21.3%**, versus 91.2% on Spider 1.0. The project site puts GPT-4o at **10.1%**, versus 86.6% on Spider 1.0. Same models, honest data, an 8.5× collapse.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On BEAVER, off-the-shelf GPT-4o scored 0.0% under the retrieval setting and 2.0% retrieval-free, and the authors said none of the off-the-shelf LLMs could answer any question correctly.
claims.quote: Off-the-shelf GPT-4o scored **0.0% under the retrieval setting and 2.0% retrieval-free**, and the authors state plainly that "none of the off-the-shelf LLMs (even GPT-4o) can answer any question correctly."

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: Snowflake's engineering team measured GPT-4o at 51% on an internal set of 150 real BI questions, meaning roughly every second answer was wrong.
claims.quote: Snowflake's engineering team [measured GPT-4o at 51%](https://www.snowflake.com/en/engineering-blog/cortex-analyst-text-to-sql-accuracy-bi/) on their internal set of 150 real BI questions - which means roughly every second answer was wrong, fluently.

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The source's table reports Snowflake improving from 51% without structure to 90%+ with a hand-authored semantic model, and dbt Labs improving from 84-90% to 98-100% with a deterministic semantic layer on an 11-question set.
claims.quote:
| Snowflake (2024) | 51% | 90%+ | Hand-authored semantic model |
| dbt Labs (2026) | 84-90% | 98-100% | Deterministic semantic layer (11-question set) |

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: The Spider 2.0 leaderboard table lists 10-21% raw performance versus 70-96% self-reported with multi-step agentic scaffolds that use schema exploration and self-correction.
claims.quote: | Spider 2.0 leaderboard (2026) | 10-21% raw | 70-96% self-reported | Multi-step agentic scaffolds with schema exploration and self-correction |

claims.question: q3
claims.claim: On a 1,400-column estate, the schema may not fit usefully in context, and the model must guess which schema subset matters before writing SQL, with a wrong guess being unrecoverable.
claims.quote: On a 1,400-column estate, the schema does not fit usefully in context - and even when it technically fits, relevance gets diluted. The model must _guess which subset of the schema matters_ before it writes a line of SQL, and a wrong guess at that step is unrecoverable.
